name: IMPROVEMENT COMPANY LOBBY
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE CHAIRS
LOOK_AT: Six chairs, each more comfortable than anything else in the territory. A man could wait here all day, and that is the design.
The cushions are plumped after every visitor. I have watched the clerk do it, tenderly.
Each one faces the inner door. You wait looking at the thing you are waiting for.
LISTEN_TO: Upholstery, accepting someone's shape. It approves of everyone.
Leather, settling. That is the sound of somebody deciding to stay a bit longer.
A long, comfortable exhale of horsehair. It is the sound of an afternoon going missing.

LOOK_AT: Six chairs, and for the first time in Company history, nobody waiting in any of them. Comfort with no takers. It is the saddest furniture in the territory and I cannot spare it a full minute.

overrides.USE: I sat. Twenty minutes evaporated. These chairs are how the Company buys time — literally, in bulk, from visitors.

subjects.name: THE CARPET
LOOK_AT: An actual carpet, red as a promise, freighted a thousand miles so that boots could apologize for themselves at the door.
Turkish, or claiming to be. The only floor covering in Consolation, and it goes right up to the mud at the threshold.
A path is worn in it from the street door to the inner door, and nowhere else. Nobody wanders in here.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It swallows footsteps whole. You could be robbed here politely and not hear it coming.
Nothing. It takes my footsteps and keeps them.
A faint grit underfoot by the door, where the territory got in.

overrides.PULL: It runs under the desk, under the door, and — for all I know — under the town.

subjects.name: THE PORTRAIT OF FANSHAWE
LOOK_AT: The Colonel, in oils, one hand on a globe. The globe is turned so his thumb covers the East.
The painter has given him a kindly eye and a firm jaw and charged, I imagine, for both.
A brass plate below it: COL. A. FANSHAWE, FOUNDER. The rank is engraved deeper than the name.
LISTEN_TO: Canvas. Even the painting says nothing without an appointment.
The frame ticks against the wall when the inner door opens. He knows when somebody is going in.
Nothing. An oil portrait at rest is the most patient listener in the building.

overrides.PUSH: Straightened it. It was straight. It is now very slightly crooked and I feel I have accomplished something.
overrides.USE: I spun it. His thumb-mark is worn into it over the East. I stopped spinning it.

subjects.name: THE PROSPECTUS RACK
LOOK_AT: Pamphlets: CONSOLATION — TERRITORY OF TOMORROW. The artist has drawn the town with a river it does not have, running gold it has not got.
On the back of each pamphlet, a small form: I WISH TO INVEST $___ IN TOMORROW. Several have been filled in and not mailed.
The river in the drawing has a steamboat on it now. Each edition, the town gets more water.
LISTEN_TO: Paper, riffling in the door's draft. Optimism, ventilated.
A pamphlet slipping down in its slot, settling into a better position.
Nothing. Tomorrow keeps very quiet in print.

LOOK_AT: The rack is empty. TERRITORY OF TOMORROW went out of print somewhere between the filing and the morning after.
LISTEN_TO: The draft, unemployed.

overrides.PICK_UP: Free, insists the clerk. Nothing in this building is free. I took one. We shall see what it cost.

subjects.name: THE CLOCK
LOOK_AT: A fine clock, eleven minutes slow. In this building, your appointment is always slightly sooner than you think, and you are always slightly late.
The clerk winds it every morning, carefully, so that it stays eleven minutes slow.
Brass pendulum, walnut case. It is the best-made lie in the room, and it has competition.
LISTEN_TO: It ticks with authority. Wrong, but with authority.
Tick. Tick. Wrong, wrong, with conviction.
The chime, gathering itself. It will strike eleven minutes after the town has gone to lunch.

overrides.USE: Setting it right would be an act of vandalism against a working system.

subjects.name: THE RECEPTION DESK
LOOK_AT: High enough that you address the clerk's collar. Papers pass over it in one direction only.
A brass bell on the desk, polished, with no sign it has ever been rung. The clerk sees you coming.
The clerk's book is open at today. My name is in it already, with the time I arrived: eleven minutes early.
LISTEN_TO: A pen nib, somewhere behind the panelling, writing without pause.
The pen nib again, behind the panelling, steady as rain.
The clerk, breathing through his nose with the patience of a professional.

subjects.name: THE DOOR TO THE OFFICE
LOOK_AT: Panelled, brass-handled, and it opens for you exactly when the Colonel finds it useful. I have watched men age in front of it.
The handle is polished on the inside of the curve, where the Colonel's hand goes, and dull where a visitor would reach.
A pane of frosted glass at head height, through which nothing can be seen and everything is suggested.
LISTEN_TO: Voices, shaped like laughter, sized like arithmetic.
A laugh behind it, generous and long. Somebody is being given something.
Nothing. Then the latch, and the door opens exactly as I look away from it.

subjects.name: THE WINDOW BLINDS
LOOK_AT: Half-drawn, always, at the same angle. The Company sees the street; the street sees slats.
The slats are dusted. The window behind them is not.
Through the slats, the street in strips: a horse's head, a wheel, a man's boots, and nothing whole.
LISTEN_TO: A tap when the wind moves them. The building's one nervous habit.
A slat ticking in the draft from the door.
The street, cut into slices and served politely.

subjects.name: THE SPITTOON, POLISHED
LOOK_AT: A spittoon polished to a shine that forbids its purpose. Nobody has ever dared.
My face is in it, warped and improved. It is a very flattering spittoon.
There is a small brass plaque on it, which says PRESENTED, and nothing else.
LISTEN_TO: A ring, faint, like a bell that regrets being one.
A hum when the door closes, tuned more or less to F.
Nothing. It has never been used, and it has never looked better.

subjects.name: THE MAP OF HOLDINGS
LOOK_AT: The district again, but coloured: what the Company owns is green, and the map is mostly green. My claim is a small white apology near the edge.
The green is hand-tinted, and someone has gone over the edges twice, so there is no doubt where the Company ends. It does not, much.
The legend has two entries: COMPANY and OTHER. OTHER is in very small type.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. The green does not need to say anything.
Nothing. Paper with this much green on it is very composed.
The frame tapping the wall as the inner door shuts.

subjects.name: THE MODEL
LOOK_AT: A scale model of Consolation as it will be. A bank, an opera house, a second church, a park. It is beautifully made. It has been beautifully made for nine years.
The opera house has tiny painted posters on it for an opera that has not been written.
The model's Main Street is paved. The real one is three yards away and is not.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing. A town in miniature is even quieter than the real one.
A tiny bell in the model church, ringing when I knock the table. It is in tune, which is how I know it is a model.

subjects.name: THE MAP WALL
LOOK_AT: Maps to Mott's strike, framed, for sale. Eleven different maps, all of them authoritative, all of them different.
Each one is priced. The more certain the map, the higher the price, and the most certain is very expensive indeed.
I have stood in front of them for a while now. The strike has been in eleven places and I have not moved.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing. Eleven confident maps, not arguing with each other in public.
The glass of one frame humming faintly when a wagon passes.

subjects.name: THE TESTIMONIALS
LOOK_AT: Framed letters of thanks from satisfied claimholders. Four of them. I have read the dates. They are all from the first two years.
One thanks the Company 'for everything'. It does not go into detail.
There is room on the wall for forty. Somebody planned for more gratitude than arrived.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing. Thanks, framed, goes very quiet after two years.
A frame settling on its wire. Even the gratitude is sagging.

subjects.name: THE SUBSCRIPTION BOOK
LOOK_AT: Shares in the Company, at a dollar. A long list of names, and beside each a small number, and the numbers were larger nearer the top of the page.
There is a pen beside it, inked and ready. It is the only pen in town that is always inked.
The last name on the page has subscribed for one share. It is spelled carefully, as if it mattered.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
The page lifting in the warm air off the stove.
Nothing. It is waiting for the next small number.

subjects.name: THE STOVE
LOOK_AT: A stove, lit, in a lobby, in July. Nobody who comes in here is ever cold.
There are scraps of paper in the ash pan, half burned. The Company heats its lobby with what it no longer needs.
It is very warm in here. You do not want to leave, and you do not want to take your coat off, and so you sit.
LISTEN_TO: Burning. Paper, I think, rather than wood.
A soft collapse in the firebox as something settles.
Burning, steadily. It is never allowed to go out, which is the most expensive thing in the room.
